@graph.headline: AWS Bedrock AgentCore Architecture: Production Patterns for Enterprise AI Agents
@graph.description: A comprehensive guide to building production-ready AI agents on AWS using Bedrock, AgentCore, and the Strands framework. Learn the architectural patterns, security controls, and operational best practices that power enterprise agent deployments.
@graph.abstract: AWS Bedrock provides an enterprise foundation for AI agents through Bedrock Agents, AgentCore runtime, and the open-source Strands framework. Deep IAM integration, automated guardrails, and persistent DynamoDB memory enable production workloads with strict compliance.

mainEntity.name: What are the three agent tiers in AWS Bedrock?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bedrock Agents for managed workflows, AgentCore for framework-agnostic execution, and Strands for multi-agent orchestration.

mainEntity.name: How does AWS Bedrock enforce security?

acceptedAnswer.text: Through native AWS IAM roles, VPC private endpoints, and automated Guardrails that filter harmful inputs and data leaks.

mainEntity.name: How is agent memory managed on AWS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bedrock utilizes managed session storage backed by DynamoDB, preserving conversation history and user preferences across sessions.

mainEntity.name: What is the latency impact of Bedrock Guardrails?

acceptedAnswer.text: Guardrails typically add 100 to 200 milliseconds per request, with options for asynchronous evaluation in high-speed pipelines.

mainEntity.name: Can Bedrock agents call third-party APIs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, via OpenAPI schema action groups that invoke AWS Lambda functions to communicate securely with external services.
